Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

CONCERNING

a. that women and children are beings created by Almighty God who have noble rights and dignity in accordance with their nature as human beings; b. that there are still many women and children who do not fully receive their basic rights, especially women and children victims of violence; c. that all forms of violence against women and children constitute violations of Human Rights, so that women and children victims of violence need to receive protection; d. that the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, is one of the obligations that must be carried out by the Regional Government as one of the efforts to realize the welfare of the community; e. that to realize protection for women and children victims of violence in an integrated and sustainable manner, institutional support and legislation are needed that can guarantee its implementation in a coordinated and directed manner; In View of : :

Article 4

The scope of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, includes:

a. implementation of protection for women and children, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. institutional arrangements and mechanisms for implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 19

Every person who deliberately allows the occurrence of violence against women and children and/or fails to report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 15

The Business World may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 20

(1) Every person who discloses the whereabouts of victims of violence who are being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to implement protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 21

Organizers or managers of P2TPA and/or Safe Houses who are proven to collect fees from victims of violence shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.

d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and

(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 4

The scope of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, includes:

a. implementation of protection for women and children, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. institutional arrangements and mechanisms for implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 19

Every person who deliberately allows the occurrence of violence against women and children and/or fails to report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 15

The Business World may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 20

(1) Every person who discloses the whereabouts of victims of violence who are being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to implement protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 7

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 20

(1) Every person who discloses the whereabouts of victims of violence who are being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to implement protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 4

The scope of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, includes:

a. implementation of protection for women and children, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. institutional arrangements and mechanisms for implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence.

6.1.text:
Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 4

The scope of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, includes:

a. implementation of protection for women and children, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. institutional arrangements and mechanisms for implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 23

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 7

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 17

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 15

The Business World may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Part One

General

Part One

General

Article 20

(1) Every person who discloses the whereabouts of victims of violence who are being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to implement protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 19

Every person who deliberately allows the occurrence of violence against women and children and/or fails to report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER IV

SCOPE

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

6.6.text:
Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 15

The Business World may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 4

The scope of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, includes:

a. implementation of protection for women and children, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. institutional arrangements and mechanisms for implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 19

Every person who deliberately allows the occurrence of violence against women and children and/or fails to report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 15

The Business World may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 20

(1) Every person who discloses the whereabouts of victims of violence who are being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to implement protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Article 3

The purpose of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, is to ensure the protection of women and children, so they do not become victims of violence and to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of women and children and their families, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.

Article 4

The scope of implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, includes:

a. implementation of protection for women and children, whether before, during or after violence occurs, as well as prevention so that violence does not occur;
b. institutional arrangements and mechanisms for implementing protection for women and children, especially victims of violence.

Article 7

(1) The organizer of protection, prevention, safeguarding and handling of women and children, especially victims of violence is carried out in an integrated manner, covering legal, medical, medicolegal and psychosocial aspects, by the Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment (P2TP2A)

or other name that has the same functional role as P2TP2A. (2) The P2TP2A institution and or other similar name shall be established by Decree of the Regent.

(3) The implementation of P2TP2A services and or other names shall be conducted in accordance with Minimum Service Standards (SPM) and Standard Operating Procedures (SOP) in accordance with statutory provisions.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 14

(1) The community may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection of women and children, victims of violence especially for women, children and their families.

(2) Community members who know, hear, and see the occurrence of violence are obligated to provide assistance and protection to victims of violence especially women, children and their families.

Article 23

At the time this Regional Regulation is stipulated and promulgated, all provisions related to the protection of women and children, especially victims of violence, shall remain in force insofar as they are not contrary to this Regional Regulation.

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 15

The Business World may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN, ESPECIALLY VICTIMS OF VIOLENCE

Article 16

(1) Financing for the implementation of protection of women and children, prevention, safeguarding and handling of victims of violence, especially women and children, shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency, through the SKPD responsible for women and children protection affairs.

(2) Budget management for the implementation of protection of women and children victims of violence shall be conducted with the principles of justice, efficiency, transparency and accountability.

Article 19

Every person who deliberately allows the occurrence of violence against women and children and/or fails to report the occurrence of violence against women and children, shall be subject to sanctions as regulated in the applicable laws and regulations.

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 13

In coordinating the implementation of protection for victims of violence especially for women, children and their families, the Regional Government appoints the Regional Government Work Unit (SKPD) in charge of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection as coordinator.

Article 20

(1) Every person who discloses the whereabouts of victims of violence who are being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to implement protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

Article 15

The Business World may play a role in carrying out obligations and responsibilities towards the implementation of protection for victims of violence, especially for women, children and their families.

Article 10

Regional Government, community, and business sector are obligated and responsible for the implementation of protection of women and children, especially victims of violence and their families.

Article 17

(1) Evaluation, reporting and accountability by P2TP2A or other similar names as the institution implementing protection for women and children victims of violence shall be conducted periodically to the Regent.

(2) The mechanism for evaluation, reporting and supervision of the implementation of protection for women and children, especially victims of violence, shall be regulated by a Regent's Decree.

Article 6

(1) Prevention services are all forms of services provided to all communities in general, especially women and children both legally, socially, culturally and economically that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(2) Protection services are all forms of services provided to communities especially women and children who have vulnerability to become victims of violence, due to their situation and condition as well as their families. Services provided include legal, social, cultural and economic services that impact the enhancement of knowledge, skills and awareness so as not to become victims and perpetrators of violence.

(3) Handling services, include all forms of minimum services both legal, medical, psychosocial services, rehabilitation and social reintegration provided to women and children who become victims of physical, psychological, sexual violence, trafficking in women and children, neglect, and exploitation.

(4) Procedures, mechanisms and service standards for prevention, protection and handling, as referred to in paragraphs (1), (2) and (3) shall be further regulated by Regent Regulation.

Part Four

Form and Mechanism of Prevention and Protection Services Article 8

(1) Formulation of policies, program planning and budgeting for prevention and protection services shall be implemented through mechanisms: a. mapping, collection, processing and presentation of data on women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence; b. coordination and synchronization of program planning with relevant SKPD;

c. preparation of programs and activities supported by budgeting; and

d. establishment of programs and activities in planning documents. (2) Implementation of prevention and protection of women and children in general and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be implemented through mechanisms:

a. implementation of programs and activities contained in SKPD budgeting documents;
b. coordination and synchronization of program and activity implementation with relevant SKPD; and
c. monitoring, evaluation and reporting on policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children. (3) Mechanisms for formulating policies, programs and activities and services shall be further regulated in minimum service standards and standard operating procedures in Regent Regulation.
(4) Formulation of policies, programs and activities for the implementation of protection of women and children vulnerable to becoming victims of violence shall be coordinated by the SKPD in charge of Regional Development Planning.
(5) Prevention and protection efforts for women and children in general and those vulnerable to victims shall be implemented by: a. establishing work networks in violence prevention efforts; b. conducting coordination, integration, synchronization of violence prevention based on partnership patterns among stakeholders; c. establishing violence prevention systems, mapping locations or areas prone to violence; and
d. conducting socialization on prevention of violence against women, as well as fulfillment of the rights of children and women.

Article 5

(1) The implementation of protection for women, children and families who are victims of violence constitutes a comprehensive prevention system, covering protection against all forms of violence, trafficking of women and children, economic exploitation, sexual exploitation, maltreatment, neglect and or abandonment in all situations including women and children with disabilities, children of migrant worker families, children in conflict with the law, children in emergency situations and those vulnerable to becoming victims of violence.

(2) The regional government is obligated and responsible for implementing protection against all forms of violence against women and children and their families. .

Article 20

(1) Every person who discloses the whereabouts of victims of violence who are being placed in a confidential location, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 3 (three) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).

(2) In the event that the act as referred to in paragraph (1) is committed by an official appointed to implement protection, shall be threatened with imprisonment for a maximum of 6 (six) months or a maximum fine of Rp. 50,000,000,- (fifty million rupiah).
